## DIY earplug recipes are not safe to provide

No household recipe can be responsibly designated medical-grade, hypoallergenic, odor-free, or skin-neutral for insertion into the ear. A mixture that seems soft or non-irritating can swell, break apart, trap moisture, injure the canal or eardrum, or be difficult to remove. Paraffin wax and beeswax are not safe DIY earplug ingredients; neither is a substitute for earwax.

For protection, use a purpose-made product:

| Need | Safer choice | Initial suitability |
|---|---|---|
| Noise | Tested disposable foam earplugs, fitted as their label directs | High when correctly fitted; check the package’s NRR or SNR rating |
| Reusable noise protection | Purpose-made silicone or thermoplastic earplugs | Moderate to high; follow cleaning and replacement instructions |
| Music or communication | Filtered or communication earplugs made for that use | Use the specified product; attenuation varies |
| Swimming | Swim plugs specifically labeled for water protection, or professionally fitted swim plugs | High for surface swimming when correctly fitted |
| Noise and water | Separate products for each activity unless a product is explicitly rated for both | Do not assume one rating covers both |

Keep putty-style swim plugs at the ear opening; don’t push them into the canal. Don’t use earplugs for diving unless the product and a clinician specifically confirm they’re appropriate. If you have ear tubes, a perforated eardrum, pain, discharge, or recurring infections, ask a clinician before using plugs.
